candidates.source: At first, I just kept going north, but I ran into a huge blockade, spears and pistols and all.  I started going up to check it out, and before I knew it they were opening fire!  I coulda died, but I still have pretty good reactions.  I turned tail and rode out of there.  My horse had taken some bad hits though, and I found out the hard way when he stumbled and fell and I broke my ass.  Made it a few miles before I wound up stuck in the ass-end of nowhere.  I settled in to wander.  I guess I'm still kinda heading north, just by a pretty round-about way, you know?
candidates.target: 起初，我只是继续向北走，但我遇到了一个巨大的封锁线，有长矛和手枪之类的。我开始上前探查，没想到他们开火了！我本可以死掉的，但我的反应还算快。我掉头就跑，骑着马逃离了那里。不过我的马中了几枪，我硬是骑着它跑了几英里，结果在一个偏远的地方摔了一跤，把屁股摔伤了。我只能四处游荡了。我想我还是大致朝北走，只是走得有点弯弯绕绕的，你知道的。

candidates.source: Anyway, long story short, I were headin' back up to Mount Greenwood to check on th'old campin' place again when I heard all that trouble start.  Decided to camp out there to see it all through, but it didn't ever end, now, did it?  So here I am.
candidates.target: 总之，我本来要回格林伍德山去看看老营地的，结果半路听说那边有麻烦，就决定在那里扎营看个究竟。谁知道这麻烦一直没完，所以我就一直留在这里。

candidates.source: Anyway, long story short, I were headin' back up to Mount Greenwood to check on th'old campin' place again when I heard all that trouble start.  Decided to camp out there to see it all through, but it didn't ever end, now, did it?  So here I am.
candidates.target: 总之，长话短说，我正打算返回绿木山去再看看那个旧营地，然后就听到了所有那些麻烦事开始。我决定在那里露营，看看事情的结局，但它似乎永远没有结束，是吧？所以，我在这里。

candidates.source: Anyway, long story short, I were headin' back up to Mount Greenwood to check on th'old campin' place again when I heard all that trouble start.  Decided to camp out there to see it all through, but it didn't ever end, now, did it?  So here I am.

candidates.source: That was when I had my old pistol, the blue one.  We called 'er ol' yeller on account of the war.  One time me an' Marty Gumps - or, as he were known to me, Rusty G - were messin' with ol' yeller up Mount Greenwood in the summertime, lookin' fer something to shoot and some fireflies to catch.

candidates.source: *shrugs, looking distant.  "I don't really like to talk about that time much.  None of us do.  Short story is that I made it to one of the evacuation shelters and got loaded onto a bus.  It was supposed to go to some sort of FEMA support camp, but there was a roadblock on the way there.  A few people just jumped out and ran for the military for protection.  They… it… it was bad.  The driver managed to get us turned around and booked it, and I guess they didn't chase us.  She took us back to one of the shelters and we found the address for this place.  Only a few of us decided to risk it, the rest stayed at the shelter to try their luck a different way.  I still wonder how they did."
candidates.target: 他耸耸肩，目光空洞。“我真的不太想多提那段时间的事。我们都一样。简单来说，我赶到了一个疏散避难所，然后上了公交车。车上说要去一个什么应急支援营地，但半路上有路障。有几个人直接跳车跑去找军队保护。他们……那情况……很糟。司机设法调转车头开走，我想他们没追上来。她把我们带回了避难所，我们找到了这个地方的地址。只有少数人决定冒险来这里，其他人留在避难所另寻他法。我还是想知道他们过得怎么样。”

candidates.source: At first, I just kept going North, but I ran into a huge military blockade.  They even had those giant walking robots like on TV.  I started going up to check it out, and before I knew it they were opening fire!  I coulda died, but I still have pretty good reactions.  I turned tail and rolled out of there.  My Hummer had taken some bad hits though, and I found out the hard way I was leaking gas all down the freeway.  Made it a few miles before I wound up stuck in the ass-end of nowhere.  I settled in to wander.  I guess I'm still kinda heading North, just by a pretty round-about way, you know?
candidates.target: 起初，我只是继续往北走，但我遇到了一个巨大的军事封锁线。他们甚至有像电视上那种巨大的行走机器人。我开始上前探查，没想到他们开火了！我差点没死，但我的反应还算不错。我掉头就跑，开着我的悍马逃离了那里。不过我的悍马中了好几枪，我发现自己沿着高速公路漏油了。我开了几英里，最终困在了荒郊野外。我只好开始漫无目的的游荡。我想我还是大致往北走，只是方式有点迂回，你懂的？

I started going up to check it out, and before I knew it they were opening fire!  I coulda died, but I still have pretty good reactions.  I turned tail and rolled out of there.  My Hummer had taken some bad hits though, and I found out the hard way I was leaking gas all down the freeway.  Made it a few miles before I wound up stuck in the ass-end of nowhere.  I settled in to wander.  I guess I'm still kinda heading North, just by a pretty round-about way, you know?

candidates.source: R.I. BILL WOULD REQUIRE POLICE SOFTWARE FIRMS TO DISCLOSE METHODS.  A bill introduced in the Rhode Island state legislature would require any company providing crime prediction software to law enforcement to submit its methodology for independent review.  The bill comes amid growing questions about the notoriously secretive Cyonage, whose AI-assisted dispatch tools are now used by more than twenty departments across New England but whose underlying methods have never been publicly disclosed.  Similar legislation in Massachusetts and Connecticut failed to advance last session after significant lobbying efforts from the technology sector.
candidates.target: R.I. 法案将要求警方软件公司披露方法。 罗德岛州议会提出的一项法案将要求任何向执法机构提供犯罪预测软件的公司提交其方法供独立审查。 这项法案出台之际，人们对臭名昭著的保密公司Cyonage越来越多地提出质疑，该公司的人工智能辅助调度工具目前在新英格兰的二十多个部门中使用，但其基本方法从未公开披露。 马萨诸塞州和康涅狄格州类似的立法在去年的会议中未能通过，当时技术领域进行了大量游说。

candidates.source: In light of the facility-wide quarantine and recent developments, mutagen tests may from now on be conducted with direct personnel-subject contact if disposable equipment is not available.  All personnel directly involved in such tests are to keep a detailed self-checkup diary including basic biometric data (height, weight, color of eyes, skin pigmentation), report any observed phenotypical changes, and to submit to biweekly medical evaluations.  Remains of test subjects and affected personnel are to be processed on-site and stored in tamper-proof biohazard containers until further notice.
candidates.target: 鉴于全设施隔离和近期事态发展，如果没有可丢弃设备，现在可以进行直接接触人员的突变原检测。所有直接参与此类检测的人员必须保持详细的自我健康记录，包括基本生物测量数据（身高、体重、眼睛颜色、皮肤色素沉着），报告任何观察到的表型变化，并接受每两周一次的医疗评估。测试对象和受影响人员的遗骸必须在现场处理，并存放在防篡改的生物危险容器中，直到另行通知。

candidates.source: All three are easy to locally produce in significant quantities and are non-perishable.  We have a local farmer or two and a few hunter types that have been making attempts to provide us with the nutritious supplies.  We do always need more suppliers though.  This stuff is rather cheap in bulk, so I can pay a premium for any you have on you.  Canned food and other edibles are handled by the merchant in the front in trade.

candidates.source:
To produce one unit of stormwrought blood, you need twenty-five liters of blood.  Any blood a vampire can feed from will do, but you must not mix different blood types or else the ritual will fail.

This ritual needs to be done within five meters of a tear in reality, or the blood will fail to attune to its energies.

When the ritual will be completed, a storm charged with the same energies will begin.  Stay in it until the blood is simmering and it'll be ready to be used.  Do not worry if it doesn't fully charge the first time for these storms are frequently seen these days.
candidates.target:
制作一单位风暴血，你需要二十五升血。任何吸血鬼可以吸食的血都可以，但你不能混搭不同的血型，否则仪式会失败。

这个仪式需要在现实裂缝五米范围内进行，否则血无法与能量共鸣。

当仪式完成时，一场充满相同能量的风暴将会开始。待在风暴中直到血开始沸腾，就可以使用了。不用担心第一次不能完全充能，因为这种风暴现在经常出现。

candidates.source: Actually, yeah.  It's a long shot but we could follow it if you like.  I ran into another survivor once - don't think she made it, she was heading to a nearby mall, and that place was overrun.  She mentioned seeing a guy taking care of his cabin in the woods though.  Said she thought about checking on him, but that was when things were all going nuts, and she decided against it.  I got some directions and never followed through on it.
candidates.target: 其实，是的。这是一个很渺茫的可能性，但如果你喜欢，我们可以去试试。我之前遇到过另一个幸存者——我不确定她是否活下来了，她当时正朝着附近的商场走去，但那里已经被占领了。她提到看到一个男人正在森林中的小屋里照顾东西。她说她想去看看他，但那时情况很混乱，她最终放弃了这个想法。我得到了方向，但从未去过。

Said she thought about checking on him, but that was when things were all going nuts, and she decided against it.  I got some directions and never followed through on it.
candidates.target: 其实，是的。这希望渺茫，但如果你愿意，我们可以去试试。我曾经遇到过另一位幸存者——我想她没能活下来，她当时正前往附近的一家商场，而那里已经被彻底攻陷。不过她提到，曾看到有个男人在树林里照料他的木屋。她说自己本来想去看看他，但那时局势已经彻底失控，她最终打消了这个念头。我拿到了去那里的路线，却一直没去成。

candidates.source: &Still completely mute, it shows you something you had initially missed.  The entire wall behind the workbench is full of various weapons; some as big as modern rifles, a few as large as the machine guns installed on aircraft, and one that looks like a dismantled tank turret.  Melee weapons were not forgotten, from moderately-sized swords and clubs to war hammers twice the height of a human, and what you can describe only as "boots for mecha".  Then it points to a sign near you that shows three things: the carved pictograms of coins, some sign you are not familiar with, and a pictogram of a bullet - all things considered, this creature is either a weaponmaster, or a weapon merchant.
candidates.target: 仍然一言不发，它向你展示了你最初错过的东西。工作台后面的整面墙上都挂满了各种武器；有些像现代步枪那么大，少数几件像安装在飞机上的机枪那么大，还有一件看起来像拆解了的坦克炮塔。近战武器也没被遗忘，从中等大小的剑和棍棒到高过人两倍的战锤，还有你只能描述为“机械战甲靴”的东西。然后它指了指你身边的标志，上面显示了三样东西：刻着硬币的图标、一个你不熟悉的符号，以及一个子弹的图标——综合来看，这家伙要么是武器大师，要么是武器商人。

candidates.source: They run this place, and they don't run a charity.  We get paid for working around the place, maintaining it, what have you, and we trade cash for food.  The thing is, supply and demand and all… there's a lot more cash than food around.  It's easier to buy a laptop than a piece of beef jerky, and there's no sign of that getting better.  The balance is way off right now, a hard day of work barely gets you enough to fill your belly.  I shouldn't bitch too much though.  I don't know much better way to run it, although rumor is that the folks living downstairs have it a lot easier than we do.  I try not to think too much on that.
candidates.target: 他们管理这个地方，这可不是慈善机构。我们工作、打理这里，等等，我们用现金换取食物。问题是，供需关系导致现金比食物多得多。买一台笔记本电脑比买一块牛肉干容易多了，而且这种情况似乎不会有改善。目前平衡度很差，辛苦一天工作赚来的钱刚好够填饱肚子。我不应该抱怨太多，我不知道还有更好的管理方式，尽管有传言说楼下的人比我们好过多了。我尽量不去多想。

The thing is, supply and demand and all… there's a lot more cash than food around.  It's easier to buy a laptop than a piece of beef jerky, and there's no sign of that getting better.  The balance is way off right now, a hard day of work barely gets you enough to fill your belly.  I shouldn't bitch too much though.  I don't know much better way to run it, although rumor is that the folks living downstairs have it a lot easier than we do.  I try not to think too much on that.
candidates.target: 他们管着这个地方，而且他们可不是来做慈善的。我们得在这工作挣钱，维护整个中心正常运作，诸如此类，然后用现金交换食物。问题是，由于供需关系……现金比食物要多得多。买一台笔记本电脑比买一块牛肉干更容易，而且没有迹象表明这一切会好转。现在的平衡关系早被打破，一天的艰苦工作几乎都没法让你吃饱。不过，我不该抱怨太多。我可没有更好的方法来管理这里，尽管有传言说住在楼下的人比我们过得要容易得多。我尽量不去想太多。

candidates.source: Spent the remainder of her life assisting one adventurer party or another.  Eventually her luck ran out when she became ill after starvation led her to eat whatever she could forage from the woods.  The party she was with deemed her a lost cause and put a bullet in her head instead of letting her turn.  She had suffered from a treatable form of marasmus.
candidates.target: 她把余生都花在帮助一个又一个探险队上。最终，她的运气用尽，在饥饿至极的情况下，她只能在森林里采集食物充饥。她所在的探险队认为她已经无药可救，于是开枪打死了她，而不是让她变成僵尸。她患了一种可以治疗的营养不良症。

candidates.source: Well, I lived pretty well out in the middle of nowhere.  We heard about the shit goin' down, but we didn't see much of it until those men with spears came blazing through and tried to set up a camp there.  They wanted to bottle us all up, and I wasn't having with that, so my dog Buck and I, we headed out while they were all sniffin' their own farts.
candidates.target: 好吧，我住在偏远的地方，生活得还不错。我们听说了那些事情，但直到那些拿着长矛的男人冲进来试图在那里建立营地，我们才亲眼见到。他们想把我们都困住，我不干，于是我和我的狗巴克一起离开了，当时他们都在闻自己的屁味。

I take your goods - Cody would call it labor - and exchange it for the new universal currency.  If you want to convert currency I'm happy to facilitate, but it'll take a few days and there is a service charge.

candidates.source: THEY'RE NOT RIOTS!  According to head officials at the Centers for Disease Control, functional MRI studies of rioters have fit autopsy data that suggests these people are under the influence of some sort of mind-altering agent causing erratic, violent behavior.  A source inside the CDC, who did not wish to be named, informed our reporter "It's not just the rioters.  They're the heaviest affected, but we scanned our own brains when we found out.  It's everyone.  It's in me, and you.  It's in the government.  The military.  God help us all."
candidates.target: 它们不是骚乱！根据疾病控制中心高层官员的说法，对骚乱者进行的功能性磁共振成像研究与尸检数据相符，表明这些人受到某种改变思维的物质的影响，导致他们出现异常、暴力的行为。一位不愿透露姓名的疾病控制中心内部人士向我们的记者透露：“不仅仅是骚乱者。他们受影响最重，但当我们发现时，我们也扫描了我们自己的脑部。是每个人。它在我和你身上。它在政府和军队中。上帝保佑我们所有人。”

candidates.source:
Prepare subject with 800 U mutagen
Apply 500 U primer compound
Observe for 6 hours
Results: Subject rapidly grew feathers across whole body, including hands, arms, armpits, back and neck.  Some grew in unexpected places, including a few around subject's eyes, but were safely removed by the subject
Long term results: subject found themselves able to split their vision.
candidates.target:
准备主题，使用800 U突变原
应用500 U启动复合物
观察6小时
结果：主题在全身迅速长出羽毛，包括手、手臂、腋下、背部颈部。有些羽毛长在意想不到的地方，包括主题眼睛周围的几根，但已被主题安全移除。
长期结果：主题发现自己能够分裂视力。

candidates.source: You can build a faction camp in a mansion.  You have four different starting positions available, namely the Fountain Garden, Dance Floor Room, Basketball Room, and Garden with Columns. candidates.target: 或许你能给我们弄点好东西来——当然不是字面意义上的“茶”。那是我的盎格鲁街头俚语。我指的是能让你在手术中入睡的东西。大灰说你们管这叫“麻醉剂”。你们给我们一千单位麻醉剂，我们就用线把你们缝好，一切搞定。

candidates.source: “Woe to the Defeated!” \n— Brennus, Gaulish chieftain who had seized Rome (with the exception of a garrison on Capitoline Hill). When Camillus arrived from Veii and besieged him, he negotiated his withdrawal for 1000 pounds of gold, but not without using false weights and adding the weight of his sword on the scale when the Romans complained (Polybius, “Histories”, II. 18)
candidates.target: “失败者可悲！” \n—— 凯尔特人首领布伦努斯，他占领了罗马（除了卡比托利欧山上的驻军）。当卡密勒斯从威尼人那里赶来，开始围困他时，他协商以一千磅黄金换取撤退，然而，他用假的砝码，并在罗马人抱怨时，把自己的宝剑加在秤上（波里比阿，《历史》，第二卷，18章）

candidates.source: “Woe to the Defeated!” \n— Brennus, Gaulish chieftain who had seized Rome (with the exception of a garrison on Capitoline Hill). When Camillus arrived from Veii and besieged him, he negotiated his withdrawal for 1000 pounds of gold, but not without using false weights and adding the weight of his sword on the scale when the Romans complained (Polybius, “Histories”, II. 18)
candidates.target:
“不幸啊，战败者！”
——布伦努斯，高卢首领，曾攻占罗马（仅卡比托利欧山上有驻军）。当卡米卢斯从维埃抵达并围攻他时，他以1000磅黄金为代价谈判撤退，但当罗马人抱怨称重不公时，他还在天平上增加了自己剑的重量。（出自波吕比奥斯，《史记》，第二卷，第18篇）

candidates.source: “Woe to the Defeated!” \n— Brennus, Gaulish chieftain who had seized Rome (with the exception of a garrison on Capitoline Hill). candidates.source: “Woe to the Defeated!” \n— Brennus, Gaulish chieftain who had seized Rome (with the exception of a garrison on Capitoline Hill). When Camillus arrived from Veii and besieged him, he negotiated his withdrawal for 1000 pounds of gold, but not without using false weights and adding the weight of his sword on the scale when the Romans complained (Polybius, “Histories”, II. 18)
candidates.target: “给败者诅咒！”\n—— 布伦努斯，一位攻占罗马的盖尔人首领（除卡皮托林山上有一小队驻守外）。当卡米路从维伊来袭并包围他时，他为了1000磅黄金协商了他的撤退，但他并没有不使用虚假的秤重，并在罗马人抱怨时，在秤上增加他剑的重量（波利比乌斯，《历史》卷II.18）。

candidates.source: “Woe to the Defeated!” \n— Brennus, Gaulish chieftain who had seized Rome (with the exception of a garrison on Capitoline Hill). candidates.target: “败者当受诅咒！”——布伦努斯，高卢酋长，曾攻占罗马（仅卡比托利欧山岗上的驻军除外）。当卡米卢斯从维伊率军抵达并围困他时，他通过谈判以一千磅黄金换取撤军，但在罗马人抗议时，他使用伪造的砝码，并在天平上加上自己剑的重量以补足差额（波利比乌斯，《历史》，卷二，第 18 章）。

candidates.target: “败者当受诅咒！”——布伦努斯，高卢酋长，曾攻陷罗马（仅卡皮托利尼山岗驻守的卫队除外）。当卡米卢斯从韦伊城赶来并围困他时，布伦努斯以一千磅黄金为代价议和撤军，但在罗马人提出异议时，他竟使用虚假的秤砣，并在秤盘上加上自己剑的重量（波利比乌斯，《历史》卷二，第 18 节）。

candidates.source: “Woe to the Defeated!” \n— Brennus, Gaulish chieftain who had seized Rome (with the exception of a garrison on Capitoline Hill). When Camillus arrived from Veii and besieged him, he negotiated his withdrawal for 1000 pounds of gold, but not without using false weights and adding the weight of his sword on the scale when the Romans complained (Polybius, “Histories”, II. 18)
candidates.target: “败者有祸！”——布伦努斯，高卢酋长，曾攻占罗马（除卡比托利欧山驻军外）。当卡米卢斯从维爱抵达并围困他时，双方议定以一千磅黄金换取其撤军，但罗马人提出异议时，他并未罢休，而是使用假砝码，并在秤上加上自己剑的重量（波利比乌斯，《历史》，卷二，18 节）。

candidates.source: “Woe to the Defeated!” \n— Brennus, Gaulish chieftain who had seized Rome (with the exception of a garrison on Capitoline Hill). When Camillus arrived from Veii and besieged him, he negotiated his withdrawal for 1000 pounds of gold, but not without using false weights and adding the weight of his sword on the scale when the Romans complained (Polybius, “Histories”, II. 18)
candidates.target: “战败者之祸！” ——布伦努斯，占领罗马的高卢酋长（除卡皮托林山上的一个驻军以外）。当从维伊来的卡米卢斯将他团团围困时，他与之谈判，以1000磅黄金的作为条件，当黄金重量不足时他将自己的剑的放在了天平上，作为对罗马人抱怨的回应（波利比亚斯，《历史》，第二章）。18岁）

candidates.source: Hey, don't bogart the joint!
candidates.target:
别一个人霸着！ (Bié yī gè rén bà zhe!)

Or, more colloquially (and referencing the original meaning):

别藏着不分享！ (Bié cáng zhe bù fēnxiǎng!) - Don't hide it and not share!

The best translation depends on the context. The first is a more general "don't hog it," while the second is closer to the original drug reference.

candidates.source: Sometimes, I kinda wonder why other people *didn't* know things were going to go wrong.  Hindsight is twenty-twenty, I guess.  I'll be honest though, as much as I'd like to pat myself on the back, it wasn't me that figured it out.  When the really early riots started out, even though they were way up in the Midwest, my wife just had a bad feeling.  We'd been thinking of a getaway anyway, and I had some time off, so we took it as an excuse to get out to the cabin and wait for everything to blow over.  Here we are.  It wasn't so much knowing how things were going to go, more just straight luck that we trusted our - *her* - gut at the right time and lucked out.
candidates.target: 有时候，我不禁纳闷为什么其他人*没有*预见到事情会出错。回过头来看，一切都显而易见，我想。虽然我很想为自己感到自豪，但必须实话实说，并不是我预见了这一切。当最初的骚乱在中西部爆发时，尽管离我们很远，我妻子却有种不好的预感。我们本来就想去度假，我也正好有空，所以我们把它当作一个机会，去小木屋避一避，等一切风波平息。就这样，我们来了。这并不是因为我们知道事情会如何发展，而是纯粹的运气，我们及时相信了她的直觉，并幸运地避开了危险。

candidates.source: If you're offering.  Before everything went to hell, Jay was talking about going to some gun show.  There was a guy there who had managed to sneak some Russian gun into the US.  It was a massive deal for Jay, it was all he could talk about.  I know it's a long shot, but maybe that guy was already at the gun show?  If you find the gun you can keep it, but it would mean a lot to Jay if he could take a look.  All he wanted was to pull it apart and put it back together.
candidates.target: 如果你愿意帮忙的话，在所有事情都变得一团糟之前，杰曾说过要去某个枪展。那儿有个人成功地把一把俄罗斯枪偷偷带进了美国。这对杰来说是一件大事，他只顾着说这件事。我知道这可能性很小，但或许那个人已经在枪展上了？如果你找到了那把枪，可以留给你，但对杰来说，能看一看那把枪意义重大。他只想把它拆开然后再组装起来。

candidates.source: Okay, listen… across the hall from the bedroom… by the pillars… it's a fake wall.  Directly across the hall.  If you push in a little bit, the whole thing kinda slides aside.  I hid some guns back there and a handful of rounds, too.  I meant to bring a lot more - I had boxes on back order - but it started getting hard to buy past a certain point.  Might as well share now that we're here.  A spare bullet could save your life.
candidates.target: 好，听着... 卧室对面... 柱子旁边... 有一面假墙。 直接穿过大厅。 你轻轻一推，整个墙就会移动开。 我在那里藏了一些枪和一些子弹。 我原本打算带更多，我有好几个盒子在补货中，但过了一定时间后，买起来就很难了。 既然我们已经到了这里，还不如分享一下。 多一颗子弹可能就能救你一命。

candidates.source: Uh, well probably?  I flew fixed-wing for work, but my interest in flying was for helitack - uh, that's helicopter transport for firefighting teams.  Anyway, I got a stupid pot conviction and that disqualified me.  Took a job with the airline to keep fresh until I could finish probation and get the records sealed.  Funny, you smoke some mary jane and they say you can't save lives with firefighting.  But they'll let you fly a plane with hundreds of people in it, not like anyone's ever crashed one of those on purpose before.  So yeah, get me a helicopter and I'd be happy to fly.
candidates.target: 嗯，可能吧？我之前因为工作开过固定翼飞机，但我对飞行的热爱是针对直升机运输消防队的。总之，我因为吸毒被定罪，这让我失去了资格。我在航空公司找了一份工作，以保持我的技能，直到我完成缓刑并封存记录。有趣的是，你抽大麻他们就说你不能救火，但他们却让你驾驶载有数百人的飞机，好像从前从没有人故意撞过飞机一样。所以，是的，给我一架直升机，我很乐意驾驶。

candidates.source: We've taken every sample I can think of from Mandrake - or rather, Mandrake's gruesome reanimated corpse - and hit nothing but dead ends.  I don't think we're going to get any further.  Some mooks from admin came and packaged him up for transport to XEDRA-12, and with the new siloed information I don't know if we'll get to find out what happened to him.  We've been put under quarantine though, so that's fun.  So much for going to the movies tomorrow night.
candidates.target: 我们从曼德拉克——或者说，曼德拉克那令人作呕的复活尸体——那里拿走了所有我能想到的样本，但都死路一条。我不认为我们会再有进展了。一些行政人员过来把它打包好，准备运到XEDRA-12，有了新的隔离信息，我不知道我们是否能知道他发生了什么。我们也被隔离了，所以挺有趣的。明晚去看电影的计划泡汤了。

candidates.source: Before everything went to hell Jay was talking about going to some gun show.  There was a guy there who had managed to sneak some Russian gun into the US.  It was a massive deal for Jay, it was all he could talk about.  I know it's a long shot but maybe that guy was already at the gun show?  If you find the gun you can keep it, but it would mean a lot to Jay if he could take a look all he wanted was to pull it apart and put it back together.
candidates.target: 在一切都乱套之前，杰曾说过要去一个枪展。那里有一个人设法把一把俄罗斯枪偷偷带进了美国。对杰来说，这是一件大事，他只顾着谈论这件事。我知道这可能性很小，但那个人可能已经在枪展上了？如果你找到了那把枪，你可以留着，但对杰来说，能让他随意看看就好了，他只是想把它拆开然后再组装起来。

candidates.source: That guy started a frenzy.  People were already panicked.  There was an armed guy overseeing the transport, acting like a cop but really he was just some dumb-ass kid they'd handed a rifle to.  He tried to calm things down, and I guess it actually worked for a bit, although the 'kill the infected' bunch were freaked out and were clearly ready to jump the moment the granny with the cut on her arm started frothing at the mouth.  They started acting up again when we got to the camp.  That didn't go well for them.  A few heavily armed soldiers dragged them away, and I never saw them again.

There was an armed guy overseeing the transport, acting like a cop but really he was just some dumb-ass kid they'd handed a rifle to.  He tried to calm things down, and I guess it actually worked for a bit, although the 'kill the infected' bunch were freaked out and were clearly ready to jump the moment the granny with the cut on her arm started frothing at the mouth.  They started acting up again when we got to the camp.  That didn't go well for them.  A few heavily armed soldiers dragged them away, and I never saw them again.

candidates.source: We successfully induced resin expression in subject CC-09.  Once we got it expressing, we got gallons of the stuff, designated CC-09-R1.  The first few times, it hardened within a few minutes, but we managed to isolate a few samples in sealed jars to send for spectroscopy.  It seems to harden much slower in the absence of air; what exactly catalyzes the setting remains to be seen.
candidates.target: 我们成功地诱导了受试体CC-09中的树脂表达。一旦它开始表达，我们就得到了几加仑的物质，被指定为CC-09-R1。前几次，它在几分钟内就变硬了，但我们设法在密封的罐子里分离出一些样本，以发送进行光谱分析。在没有空气的情况下，它似乎变硬得更慢；具体是什么催化了凝固过程还有待观察。

candidates.source: we're still in early stages of getting set up, but we're not overly flush for hands, that's for sure.  I don't think we'd turn many people away, of course, but besides strong hands and willing labor, we could really use someone who could cook.  I can't tell you what it'd do for morale.  You could try asking some of the people staying on the surface in the refugee center maybe, I don't think they were part of most of the original discussions about the ranch.

candidates.source: Was making her way to Ohio to search for family when she consumed a number of poisonous roots.  Over the course of three or four days she passed.  A note found with her body read, 'I wish I could have saved him.'

candidates.target: 我不知道是怎么回事，但一位清洁工在清洁实验室时意外地激活了传送门，导致各种史前生物涌入。 立即调集安保人员，但他们无法阻止清洁工被撕裂。 混乱结束后，所有史前生物都被消灭了。

I'm never gonna know what happened to them, and that busts me up bad.  They mattered to me, you know?"  His voice catches a bit, and he coughs.  "You're here though, and that helps a lot. candidates.source: The medical software didn't just analyze the blood, it triggered a government alert.  Medical staff was under orders to immediately drive any matching samples to the nearest laboratory.  That must mean the government knew!  We have the destination address.  Go there, get in, and bring back any records you can download off a computer.  Like last time, I can compensate you, and the Old Guard saw enough promise in this assignment to spare a larger sum of 60 merch.  I'm sure you're also free to lay claim to any valuables you might find at the target location.
candidates.target: 医疗软件不仅分析了血液，还触发了政府警报。医疗人员接到命令，要立即将任何匹配的样本送到最近的实验室。这意味着政府一定知道了！我们有目的地地址。去那里，进去，从电脑上下载任何能找到的记录带回来。和上次一样，我可以补偿你，老兵们认为这个任务有足够的价值，所以拨款60默奇。我确定你也可以在目标地点找到任何你可能发现的贵重物品。

candidates.source: It's a simple matter of how we teleport.  Our clothes are often made from cloth and hides from wherever we visit, and our teleporter tears living stuff apart here and there when we travel.  Some can be saved if we take care, but there's no room to store nearly enough extra.  That, and our fabricators are always busy, no time to waste on stuff we don't need for ourselves.
candidates.target: 这只是一个传送的方式问题。我们的衣服通常是由我们访问的任何地方的布料和皮革制成的，我们的传送器在我们旅行时会在这里那里撕裂活的东西。如果我们小心，有些东西可以保存下来，但几乎没有足够的额外存储空间。此外，我们的制造者总是很忙，没有时间浪费在我们自己不需要的东西上。

candidates.source: Yeah, I, uh… I know a bit about that stuff.  Hard not to empathize, especially when I know I'm not quite as hard as others, by sheer luck.  Besides, there are so few of us left now.  What's the point in wasting time judging other people for how hard they took the end of the world?
candidates.target: 是啊，我，嗯……我对这些事情有点了解。不去同情别人真是太难了，尤其是当我知道自己只是因为运气好才没有像别人那样经历那么多磨难的时候。再说了，现在我们这样的人已经不多了。花时间去评判别人对世界末日的反应有什么意义呢？

candidates.target: 是的，呃… 我对那些事儿有点了解。很难不去感同身受，尤其当我明白自己能撑到现在，纯粹是运气好。再说，现在我们剩下的人已经这么少了。没必要浪费时间去评判别人是如何承受世界末日的打击的。

candidates.source: Once I was okay leaving the bushes, I made my way to a cave I could see a ways off.  It wasn't luxury but it kept the rain and wind off and gave me a place out of sight.  I stayed there until I got hungry.  Then I took on the wanderin' life until we met.
candidates.target: 等我从灌木丛里出来后，我朝远处一个洞穴走去。那儿虽然不算豪华，但可以遮风挡雨，还能让我躲避风头。我在那里待到饿了为止。然后我又开始了流浪生活，直到我们相遇。

candidates.source: You dream you are standing on a beach under a sun, swollen and red and filling a quarter of the sky.  The air is hot, and as you watch the sun expands to fill a third of the sky, then half, then more.  As you close your eyes against the blinding light, you wake up.
candidates.target: 你梦见自己站在海滩上，头顶是一轮肿胀的、红色的太阳，占据了天空的四分之一。空气炽热难耐，你看着太阳逐渐扩大，占据了天空的三分之一，然后是二分之一，越来越大。当你因刺眼的光芒而闭上眼睛时，你醒了过来。

candidates.source: “This was the greatest action that happened in all this war, and all others that we have heard of amongst the Greeks, being to the victors most glorious and most calamitous to the vanquished. For they were utterly and at all points defeated, and their sufferings were many. Army and fleet and all they ever had perished, nothing was saved and few of so many ever returned home. Thus ended the Sicilian expedition.” \n— Thucydides (“History of the Peloponnesian War”, VII. 87.6–7)
candidates.target:
这是整个战争中最伟大的行动，也是我们从希腊人那里听说过的最辉煌的胜利，对失败者来说是最悲惨的。因为他们完全被击败，在各个方面都失败了，并且遭受了巨大的痛苦。他们的军队、舰队和他们曾经拥有的一切都毁灭了，没有什么东西被拯救，很少有这么多人能回家。西西里远征就此结束。

——修昔底德《伯罗奔尼撒战争史》，第七卷，87.6-7

candidates.source: STRANGE NEW BIOMES CONTINUE TO EXPAND.  The strange biomes of never before seen plants continue to spread.  One of the new border patrol divisions has been assigned to investigate and manage these locations that now appear all across America.  "These climate change biomes have appeared globally but we will investigate them locally," said a spokesperson for Border Patrol.  "Once we've determined the cause of these locations we will go about figuring out how to exploit or reverse these changes."

candidates.source: Well… a little while ago, I set up a radio transmitter in the radio tower not far from here, but it stopped transmitting.  I went over there and encountered some crazy stuff you wouldn't believe if you didn't see it yourself:  Some 'plants' moving around, replicating, and attacking me with lightning bolts.  Luckily, the environmental suit I've got from our employers protected me from damage, but fried my electronics.  If you're willing to back me up to eradicate them, I'll owe you a favor.  However, I suggest you turn the mission down and come back when you think you've got sufficient gear.

candidates.source: Honestly, probably better than it sounds.  I had a good bug-out bag, a nice tent, a lot of good stuff.  I hadn't suffered any internal organ damage, my stomach muscles were just really badly bruised, and I'd already had some good time to recover.  I think it kept me from doing anything too stupid, and believe me there was a high chance of that.  For a long time I had these Rambo visions of rushing into town and saving everyone, but I was still too immobile.  By the time I had my strength back, it wasn't an option… we were well into the rushing into town for supplies phase.  The closest I got to saving any old friends was putting down the monsters wearing their faces.
candidates.target: 老实说，可能比听起来要好。我有一个很好的逃生包，一个漂亮的帐篷，很多好东西。我没有受到内脏损伤，我的腹肌只是严重挫伤，我已经有足够的时间恢复了。我想这让我避免了做任何太愚蠢的事情，相信我，那可能性很高。我很长一段时间都有着像兰博一样的幻想，冲进城里拯救每个人，但我还是太不灵活了。等我恢复了体力，这已经不是一个选择了……我们已经进入了冲进城里抢物资的阶段。我离拯救老朋友最近的一次就是杀死那些戴着他们面孔的怪物。

candidates.source: I - fine.  Drugs in the water, some kind of bioweapon I guess.  You know how things were with China, they blamed it on them mostly.  Made people violent and ugly.  There were riots.  People I cared about joined them, and I guess I'll never know why.  Riots led to military and police action, which made the riots worse.  People acted like animals, not just the rioters but everyone.  Then came the monsters and nightmares walking the world like real Armageddon, and everyone died, and started coming back as monsters themselves.  There's your story.  If you want more, talk to someone else.
candidates.target: 我——还好。水里有药，某种生物武器，我猜。你知道当时和中国的情况，他们把大部分责任都归咎于中国。这让人们变得暴力和丑陋。发生了骚乱。我关心的人也加入了其中，我想我可能永远不会知道为什么。骚乱导致了军队和警察的行动，这使骚乱变得更糟。人们的行为就像动物，不仅仅是骚乱者，而是每个人。然后，怪物和噩梦开始像真实的末世一样在世界上漫游，每个人都死了，并开始自己变成怪物。这就是你的故事。如果你想要更多，去问别人吧。

SPIKE IN MENTAL HEALTH CONCERNS HAS EPIDEMIOLOGISTS WORRIED.  "There's no doubt about it," said a spokesperson from Mount Sinai Hospital.  "Hospitals over the US are overwhelmed with an increase in psychiatrically-related violent behavior such as explosivity and aggressive paranoia.  The most likely cause is a new street drug; we have yet to identify any commonality between the affected people."

Dr. Andrew Morton, a Harvard epidemiologist, has a different opinion.  "These people aren't drug users.  They're coming from all walks of life.  Sure, there's a predilection for people who already have some mental illness, but we're seeing perfectly normal people suddenly presenting with violent explosive behavior.  I think the most likely cause is infectious: no other pattern would fit this widespread an outbreak."
candidates.target:
精神健康问题激增令流行病学家担忧。"这点毫无疑问，"来自西奈山医院的发言人说道，"美国各地的医院都面临着与精神相关暴力行为的激增，如爆炸性和偏执狂。最可能的原因是一种新型的街头毒品；我们尚未在受影响的人群中找到任何共同点。"

哈佛流行病学家安德鲁·莫顿博士持有不同意见。"这些人不是吸毒者，他们来自各行各业。当然，已经患有精神疾病的人更容易受到影响，但我们看到完全正常的人突然表现出暴力的爆炸性行为。我认为最可能的原因是传染性的，其他模式无法解释如此广泛的爆发。"

candidates.source: Holy hell, the crash you recovered the black box from wasn't as old as I thought.  Check this out, it was on its approach to pick up a team sent to secure and destroy something called a 'Hazardous Waste Sarcophagus' in the middle of nowhere.  If the bird never picked up the team then we may still have a chance to meet up with them.  It includes an access code for the elevator and an encoded message for the team leader, I guess.  If we want to join up with what remains of the government then now may be our only chance.

Check this out, it was on its approach to pick up a team sent to secure and destroy something called a 'Hazardous Waste Sarcophagus' in the middle of nowhere.  If the bird never picked up the team then we may still have a chance to meet up with them.  It includes an access code for the elevator and an encoded message for the team leader, I guess.  If we want to join up with what remains of the government then now may be our only chance.

candidates.source: It's not just walking horrors and monsters that have changed with the Cataclysm.  It started a… cycle, of sorts.  Everything repeats.  We can only see it in others, but it happens to us, even you and I.  How many times have you fallen?  Your flesh rent from your body, devoured.  Or perhaps it was the quiet whimper of succumbing to the elements.  But your bones rose again.  Different flesh, different name, sometimes even different knowledge, but the bones, the same.  We are all trapped in the same cycle.  We just keep forgetting.  That's why we need to amass the Song.  That's why it has to end, even if it means the destruction, not restoration.
candidates.target: 不仅是行走的恐怖和怪物在灾难中发生了变化。它开始了一种循环，某种形式。一切都会重复。我们只能在别人身上看到它，但它也发生在我们身上，甚至你和我。你跌倒了多少次？你的肉从身体上被撕裂，被吞噬。或者也许是默默地向元素屈服的叹息声。但你的骨头又重新站了起来。不同的肉，不同的名字，有时甚至是不同的知识，但骨头，是相同的。我们都陷入了相同的循环。我们只是不断地忘记。这就是为什么我们需要积累歌曲。这就是为什么它必须结束，即使这意味着毁灭，而不是恢复。

candidates.source: Right.  Extradimensional intelligent plants with a mean streak.  They seem to have a method of traveling from reality to reality without traversing the hazards between.  Interesting, no?  I'd ask them how they do it but I don't think I could get a word in edgewise before they cut me to pieces.  I'll mark one of their groves on your map for one denarius.
candidates.target: 对。跨维度的聪明植物，有点恶毒。它们似乎有办法在不经过危险的地方就从一个现实世界旅行到另一个现实世界。有趣，不是吗？我想问问它们是怎么做到的，但我不认为我能插话，在它们把我撕成碎片之前。我会把它们树林的位置标在你的地图上，一块钱。

candidates.target: 没错。这些具有强烈个性的超维度智能植物，似乎掌握着一种穿越现实而不必经过其间危险的方法。有趣，不是吗？我想问他们如何做到的，但恐怕在他们把我撕成碎片之前，我连插嘴的机会都没有。我会在你的地图上标出其中一片林地的位置，报酬是一枚第纳尔。

candidates.source: Something changed during the Collapse - the apocalypse, if you prefer that.  The way the dead rise again and again, it's tied to their bones - notice that only when you pulp and crush them properly do they actually die.  A woman I met - Brigitte was her name - taught me how to use the power.  We call it the Song, since if you know how, you can hear it, a quiet hum in the bones.  If I collect enough Song, the concentrated power can reverse the Cataclysm.  Undo all of this.
candidates.target: 在崩塌——或者你更喜欢称其为末日——期间，有些事情发生了改变。死人不断复活的方式与他们的骨骼有关——请注意，只有在你将他们的骨骼粉碎和碾压得彻底时，他们才会真正死去。我遇到了一个叫布里吉特的女人，她教我如何使用这种力量。我们称其为“歌”，因为如果你知道如何去听，你可以在骨骼中听到一种安静的嗡嗡声。如果我收集足够多的“歌”，这种凝聚的力量可以逆转大灾难。让我们一起结束这一切。

"Don't you guys have, like, scavengers and things?"  Liam sounds like he's trying not to get irritated with Smokes.  "Can't these guys help out in some way in exchange for food?  It seems insane to just keep them sitting in your entry way."

Smokes gives him a long-suffering look.  "Like I said, ask them.  We can't take them in, though.  It's not just them.  We've had to turn away dozens of people, if we started making exceptions we'd be dead meat.  These guys are just the ones who didn't try their luck out there, they've got their reasons I guess.  I don't like this any more than you do.
candidates.target:
“你们这些人没有像清洁工之类的人吗？”利亚姆听起来有点不耐烦了。 “这些人不能以换取食物的方式提供帮助吗？让他们一直坐在你们的入口处似乎很不合理。”

斯莫克斯给利亚姆一个苦大仇深的眼神。“就像我说的，去问问他们吧。我们不能让他们进来，不仅仅是他们。我们已经拒绝了数十个人，如果我们开始破例，我们就会完蛋。这些人只是没有在外面试试运气的人，他们有他们的理由，我猜。我也不喜欢这样，和你一样。”

candidates.source:
SEARCH FOR MISSING CHILD CONTINUES

As the search continues for Theodore O'Connor, age 7, missing since last Thursday, his mother placed the blame on a goblin family in their neighborhood.  "They've been lurking around our house for days before Theo disappeared," she said during an interview on local television, "and I just know they had something to do with it.  Please bring our Theo back!"  Local community organizer Shazgra k'Morħet denounced the claims, stating, "I thought we had moved past this kind of blood libel rhetoric, but apparently rising tensions are all it takes for old accusations to resurface.  We've all seen the footage of the riots.  They're the most multicultural gatherings we've had in modern times."
candidates.target:
继续寻找失踪儿童

随着对7岁西奥多·奥康纳的搜寻持续进行，他自上周四起失踪，他的母亲将责任归咎于他们邻居的哥布林家庭。“他们在西奥多失踪前几天一直在我们家附近潜伏，”她在当地电视台的采访中说，“我只是知道他们与此有关。请把我们的西奥多带回来！”当地社区组织者沙兹格拉·克莫雷特否认了这些说法，表示：“我以为我们已经超越了这种血腥诽谤的言辞，但显然紧张局势升级，旧的指控就会再次出现。我们都看到了骚乱的录像。这是我们现代历史上最多元文化的聚会。”

candidates.source: MIT PHYSICS DEPARTMENT FACES UNPRECEDENTED FACULTY EXODUS.  The Massachusetts Institute of Technology has lost eleven tenured or tenure-track faculty members from its physics department in the past eighteen months, a rate of departure that faculty and administrators say is without precedent in the department's modern history.  The losses span nearly every subfield but have hit condensed matter and particle physics particularly hard, leaving graduate students scrambling to find new advisors.  Several described similar experiences, saying they received little notice and that departing faculty were unwilling or unable to discuss where they were going.  In at least two cases, students said their former advisors cited nondisclosure agreements and declined to say anything beyond confirming they had accepted positions outside academia.

candidates.source: No!  Dammit, no!"  Liam looks briefly panicked, then his eyes widen.  "I have something for this, hold on."  He reaches to the sofa behind him, slowly, keeping his hands away from the shotgun on the floor.  "Look.  Chris left a note."  Liam holds up the paper, in Chris' clear handwriting.  You can just make it out: it reads somewhat like a suicide note, and realization starts to dawn.  Liam nods, seeing you start to understand.  "Chris got bit while we were on our way here.  We tried to treat it, I did everything I could think of, but the infection got worse and worse.  Chris told me to just turn my back, but I couldn't do that.  We had a pact.  You know that."  Liam's eyes are red rimmed, and he wipes them with a sleeve.  "I stayed here until… until the transition.  We wrote this letter and a bunch more, stuff for Chris's family, if we can find them, you know?
candidates.target: “不！该死的，不！”利亚姆短暂地惊慌失措，然后他的眼睛睁大了。“我有办法，等等。”他慢慢地伸手到身后的沙发上，小心翼翼地避开地上的猎枪。“看，克里斯留了张纸条。”利亚姆举起纸条，上面是克里斯清晰的字体。你可以勉强看清，它看起来像是一封遗书，意识到事情的真相开始浮现。利亚姆点点头，看到你开始明白了。“克里斯在我们来的路上被咬了。我们试图治疗，我想尽了办法，但感染越来越严重。克里斯让我转过身去，但我做不到。我们有个约定，你知道的。”利亚姆的眼睛红肿，他用袖子擦了擦。“我在这里待到……直到转变。我们写了这封信和其他很多信，克里斯的家人如果能找到的话，你知道的。”

candidates.source: What, don't you remember?  No, sorry, that's not fair, it was a weird time.  OK, well, I guess this all started with the riots, didn't it?  We were just leading our lives, doing our jobs, and then people started rioting.  Not the usual protests that turned violent or anything, either, people just left their houses and started breaking shit.  The news tried to downplay it but they couldn't keep it off the internet. Well.  Well, well, well.  This is really interesting.  Look, you can see reticulations here, it looks sort of like an enlarged piece of a stipe from a basidiocarp… but look at this, these fibers are clearly unlike anything I've seen before.  I wonder if they're motile?

Okay, listen: you've got yourself a deal.  I'll come to your base, but you've gotta get me hooked up with a microscope as soon as you can.  This could be the beginning of something really cool.  Oh, and it should go without saying that I'm not coming unless you can find a place for my friends here in your base.  I'm sure you anticipated that.  Talk them into going and I'm in.  It should be easy, they're a bunch of sweet hearted saps.

candidates.source: Come a little closer, I don't want to make too much noise.  You smell much nicer than what I'm used to.  Someone in trouble banged on the door that night, she said she was desperate, she had a baby, her home had burned down and her drugs were gone and there were monsters in the streets.  We figured she was on drugs, but we couldn't turn them away so we gave them food and let them stay in the barn.
candidates.target: 靠近点，我不想太大声。你闻起来比我习惯的要好多了。那天晚上，有个人敲门，说她很绝望，有个孩子，家烧了，毒品没了，街上有怪物。我们觉得她吸毒，但不能把他们赶走，就给他们吃的，让他们在谷仓住下。

candidates.source: What, don't you remember?  No, sorry, that's not fair, it was a weird time.  OK, well, I guess this all started with the riots, didn't it?  We were just leading our lives, doing our jobs, and then people started rioting.  Not the usual protests that turned violent or anything, either, people just started breaking shit.  Some people tried to downplay it but I saw what I saw I think.  I don't know what caused it, they said it was some kind of drug or toxin in the water?  Still, I didn't really realize how bad it was getting at first.  Somewhere along the way the "rioters" started getting up and walking around with holes in their chests, and that's when the real panic took over.  The next few days - or weeks, not really sure - are a blur to me.  You'd have to ask someone else how we got from there to total collapse.
candidates.target: 什么？你不记得了？不，对不起，那时候很混乱。好吧，我想这一切都始于骚乱，对吧？我们只是过着自己的生活，做着自己的工作，然后人们开始骚乱。不是那些通常的抗议活动变暴力的情况，人们只是开始破坏东西。有些人试图淡化它，但我看到的是我看到的，我想。我不知道是什么原因，他们说水里有某种药物或毒素？尽管如此，我一开始并没有意识到情况有多糟。在某个时刻，“骚乱者”开始带着胸口的洞站起来走动，那时真正的恐慌才开始。接下来的几天——或者几周，我不太确定——对我来说是一片模糊。你得问问别人我们是如何从那时到完全崩溃的。

candidates.source: You dream of your usual patient languor being interrupted by a flash of white teeth against a carmine-soaked muzzle.  In an instant a thunderous fury overtakes you and you trumpet your rage… right before you bring that trumpeting snout, bring down those heavy spears of ivory on either side of it, down upon your attacker.  They lie, bones shattered, bleeding out their red into the icy white and causing it to steam  Just like that, your calm is restored.
candidates.target: 你梦见你平时的懒散被一闪而过的白色牙齿打断，它们背景是一张浸满鲜血的红褐色嘴吻。瞬间，雷霆般的愤怒占据了你，你怒吼着……就在你用那张吼叫的嘴吻，用那对重重的象牙尖从两侧砸向攻击者之前。它们躺在那里，骨头粉碎，鲜血流淌到冰冷的白色上，冒出热气。就这样，你的平静被恢复了。

"Aww, Muffin, have you slain a leaf or grass hopper again?" a feminine voice asks.  A cat appears in front of the door and drops a crow, dripping with black goo. "Actually she'll probably want them disinfected, and we should find her some tape too just to be on the safe side.

candidates.source: While we've managed to secure day to day food supplies, it's very much hand to mouth.  Our reserves would barely last a few days if something kept our people locked in.  We need a stockpile to avoid that.  Thanks to our outpost we have a bit of meat and vegetables coming in, but we need a better way to preserve them.  Some of our people know enough about food canning that if we had a good stock of canning jars, we could make pickles and canned meats to get us set for the winter.  I'll pay you a premium rate if you can bring us around a hundred jars to get us started.
candidates.target: 虽然我们设法确保了日常食品供应，但我们仍然是在应付眼前的事情。如果有什么事情让我们的人被困住，我们的储备只能维持几天。我们需要一个储备来避免这种情况。多亏了我们的据点，我们有点肉和蔬菜可以进来，但我们需要一个更好的方法来保存它们。我们的一些人知道如何罐装食物，如果我们有足够的罐子，我们可以制作泡菜和罐头肉，为我们准备好冬天。如果你能给我们带来大约一百个罐子让我们开始，我会给你优厚的报酬。

candidates.source: That place was chaos.  I only stayed a few hours.  They had a big backhoe running, digging a huge pit in a cordoned section they wouldn't let us near.  Well, I managed to sneak over that way, and saw them dumping load after load of the dead in the pit, pouring dirt back over them even as they revived and tried to climb out.  Even with all the shit I've seen since, it haunts me.  I knew then I had to get out.  Luckily for me, we were attacked the next morning by some giant horror, a kind I haven't really seen since then.  While the guards were busy with that, I grabbed some supplies I'd stocked up over the night and I fucked right out of there.  A few others tried to get the fuck out with me, but as far as I know I was the only lucky one.
candidates.target: 那个地方一片混乱。我只待了几个小时。他们有一台大型挖掘机在运行，在一个隔离区挖了一个巨大的坑，不让我们靠近。好吧，我设法偷偷地靠近那边，看到他们一车一车地把尸体倒入坑里，即使那些尸体复活了，试图爬出来，他们也继续往坑里倒土。即使在我看到过那么多事情之后，这仍然让我感到恐惧。我当时就知道我必须离开。幸运的是，第二天早上我们遭到了一只巨大恐怖生物的袭击，那种生物我从那以后就没再见过。当守卫们忙于对付它时，我抓住机会，拿了一些我在前一晚囤积的补给品，然后逃离了那里。有些人也试图和我一起离开，但据我所知，我是唯一一个成功的人。

Even with all the shit I've seen since, it haunts me.  I knew then I had to get out.  Luckily for me, we were attacked the next morning by some giant horror, a kind I haven't really seen since then. A few others tried to get the fuck out with me, but as far as I know I was the only lucky one.

candidates.source: Yeah.  Someone came through this way a while back saying he had tried to drive into Syracuse after the outbreak.  Didn't even make it downtown before he ran into a wall of zombies that he said could stop a tank.  He hightailed it out, but he said there were several thousand at least.  I guess when you get a bunch of them together, they end up making enough noise to attract everyone in the neighborhood.  Thankfully, we haven't had a mob like that pass by here, because I'm not sure the fence would do much to keep them out.
candidates.target: 是的。有一会儿前，有个人从这里经过，说他试图在疫情爆发之后开车去锡拉库扎。他甚至没能到达市中心，就遇到了一个僵尸墙，他说那能挡住坦克。他赶紧逃了出来，但他说至少有几千个。我想当你把他们聚集在一起时，他们最终会制造出足够的噪音来吸引附近所有人。幸好我们这里没有这样的群体经过，因为我不确定栅栏能不能把他们挡在外面。

candidates.source: I've been drawing up some plans to expand our food storage around here.  Now that we won't starve to death anytime soon, our old crates just aren't cutting it, so we're going to build a small warehouse to store everything, and I've gathered a crew to build it.  We've got most of the materials covered, but we don't have enough sheet metal to make the shelves.  If you could get us about 5,000 pounds of the stuff, I'll pay you handsomely with what we have.  How does that sound?
candidates.target: 我一直在制定计划，扩大我们这里的食物储存。现在我们不会很快饿死，所以我们旧的箱子已经不够用了，我们将建造一个小型仓库来储存一切，我已经召集了一个团队来建造它。我们已经有了大部分材料，但我们没有足够的金属板来制作货架。如果你能给我们大约5000磅的东西，我会用我们有的东西慷慨地报酬你。听起来如何？

candidates.source: &The intercom erupts into static.  Then, it resolves into a voice.  It clears its throat, then speaks slowly and carefully.  "Understood.  There is a tray embedded beneath the intercom.  Please place the drive into it."  On cue, a small portion of the wall beneath the intercom slides out along rails, revealing a large tray several inches deep.  "You are welcome to leave afterwards."

candidates.source: Depends on your definition.  I'm alive, aren't I?  When Hell itself came down from the skies and monsters started attacking the cities, I grabbed my stuff and crammed into the bunker.  My surface cameras stayed online for days; I could see everything happening up there.  I watched those things stride past.  I still have nightmares about the way their bodies moved, like they broke the world just to be here.  I had nothing better to do.  I watched them rip up the cops and the military, watched the dead rise back up and start fighting the living.  I watched the nice old lady down the street rip the head off my neighbor's dog. candidates.source:
This seems to be a digital journal of some kind.  You browse through, and in between the (frankly awful) poetry and occasional story concepts, there are a couple actual journal entries.  The first is as follows:

"Killed someone today.  An actual, living person.  Well, a maybe, on that last part.  They seemed… feral.  I panicked, and none of the group got to me quick enough, so I just… hit them.  As hard as could.  With that hammer.  I hate that it felt good."

The next readable entry mentions the author using a hammer and a large railroad spike together as a weapon.  It devolves into madness pretty quickly from there.
candidates.target:
这似乎是一本某种形式的数字日记。你浏览着，在（坦白说，很糟糕的）诗歌和偶尔的故事概念之间，有几条真正的日记条目。第一条如下：

“今天杀了个人。一个真正的、活生生的人。好吧，那最后一点可能有点疑问。他们看起来……野蛮。我惊慌失措，团队没有人及时来制止我，所以我只是……打了他们。用尽我所有的力气。用那把锤子。我讨厌那种感觉好的感觉。”

下一条可读条目提到作者用锤子和一个大铁路钉一起作为武器。从那里开始，它很快就陷入了疯狂。

“今天杀了人。一个活生生的、真实的人。嗯，后半句或许只是大概。他们看起来……像野兽。我慌了神，而我的同伴们没能及时赶到，于是我……用那把锤子狠狠砸了他们。我讨厌那种感觉竟如此令人愉悦。”

下一篇可读的条目提到作者将锤子与一根大型铁路尖钉合用作为武器。此后，故事迅速滑向疯狂。

candidates.source:
This seems to be a digital journal of some kind.  You browse through, and in between the (frankly awful) poetry and occasional story concepts, there are a couple actual journal entries.  The first is as follows:

"Killed someone today.  An actual, living person.  Well, a maybe, on that last part.  They seemed… feral.  I panicked, and none of the group got to me quick enough, so I just… hit them.  As hard as could.  With that hammer.  I hate that it felt good."

The next readable entry mentions the author using a hammer and a large railroad spike together as a weapon.  It devolves into madness pretty quickly from there.

candidates.source:
SEARCH FOR UNIVERSAL HEALING SPELL CONTINUES

Staff at Johns Hopkins University yesterday announced promising results in the long search for a health catalyst spell.  While an actual prototype formula has not been released, the draft paper indicates that animal testing showed a five percent decrease in long-term mortality rates in rats suffering from a dozen different types of cancers.  "A true universal healing catalyst spell would really be the Holy Grail", said Dr. Olivia k'Ħarzag, Director of Thaumaturgical Oncology Research at Johns Hopkins University.  "Modern cancer research's greatest limiting factor is that the most potent biomantic healing spells can only affect the caster.  If we can find a way to encourage the body's own defenses that works on a wide scale, even if we can't directly cure the cancer, we could save so many more people."
candidates.target: 约翰霍普金斯大学的工作人员昨天宣布了在长期寻找健康催化法术方面取得的令人鼓舞的结果。尽管尚未发布实际的原型配方，但论文初稿表明，动物实验显示，患有十多种不同癌症的大鼠长期死亡率降低了5%。“真正的通用治愈催化法术确实是圣杯”，约翰霍普金斯大学魔法肿瘤学研究主任奥利维亚·卡扎格博士说。“现代癌症研究最大的限制因素是，最强大的生物魔法治愈法术只能影响施法者。如果我们能找到一种方法来激发身体自身的防御机制，并在广泛范围内起作用，即使我们不能直接治愈癌症，我们也可以拯救更多的人。”

candidates.source: A young mother.  I know she was a mother, because I delivered her baby.  Sweet girl, she… she had a good sense of humor.  She came in, spitting that black goo, fighting the orderlies, dead from a spear wound through the chest.  That's when I… I don't know if I woke up, finally, or if I finally went crazy.  Either way, I broke.  I broke a lot earlier than my colleagues, and that's the only reason I lived.  I skipped out and hid for hours, while I listened to the world crumbling outside and inside.
candidates.target: 一位年轻的母亲。我知道她是母亲，因为我接生了她的孩子。甜美的女孩，她……她有很好的幽默感。她走进来，吐着黑色的粘液，与护士们搏斗，胸口中箭身亡。那时我……我不知道我是终于醒了，还是终于疯了。无论如何，我崩溃了。我比同事们早得多崩溃，这才是我活下来的唯一原因。我逃了出去，藏了好几个小时，一边听着外面和内心的世界崩塌。

candidates.source: He lives way up north, way in the middle of nowhere, with his crazy wife and my three grandkids.  Some kind of mining.  She's a bit of a hippy-dippy headcase.  I love em both though, and as far as I'm concerned they all made it out of this fucked up mess safe, out there in the boondocks.  I guess they think I'm dead, so they'll steer clear of this hellhole, and that's the best as could be.

candidates.source: Well, I lived on the edge of a small town.  Corner store and a gas station and not much else.  We heard about the shit goin' down in the city, but we didn't see much of it until the military came blazing through and tried to set up a camp there.  They wanted to bottle us all up in town, and I wasn't having with that, so my dog Buck and I, we headed out while they were all sniffin' their own farts.
candidates.target: 好吧，我住在一个小镇的边缘。有个小商店和一个加油站，别的没什么。我们听说了城市里发生的事，但直到军队开进来试图在那里建立营地，我们才亲眼见到。他们想把我们都困在镇上，我不干，于是我和我的狗巴克一起离开，趁他们自说自话的时候。

candidates.source: She lived desperately in the Cataclysm for a few years before meeting a male survivor while digging through a dumpster.  Both were wary of one another and were soon at each other's throats.  Neither side secured a victory.  Wounded and scarred, they each went to their respective hideouts.  Not long after, they met again.  The man initiated a conversation with her, asking for her help.  It was foolish to fight when they could work together instead.  She acquiesced.  In this cruel and forlorn world, they soon fell in love.  If they had each other, everything would be all right.  Decades passed and they grew old holding hands.  One day, the husband fell ill, and with his dying breath, he said he was happy all these years with her.  Stay strong without me.  The wife wept and laid down beside her husband.  Without you, nothing else matters.  She swallowed a bitter poison and departed this world to find her husband who was waiting for her.
candidates.target: 她在浩劫中绝望地生活了几年，直到她在翻找垃圾桶时遇到了一个男性幸存者。他们彼此警惕，很快就争吵起来。双方都没有取得胜利。受伤并留下伤疤后，他们各自回到了自己的藏身处。不久之后，他们再次相遇。那男人主动和她交谈，请求她的帮助。他们合作比战斗更明智。她同意了。在这个残酷而凄凉的世界里，他们很快就相爱了。只要他们在一起，一切都会好起来的。几十年过去了，他们手牵手变老。一天，丈夫病了，在临终时，他说他这些年一直很幸福。妻子哭了，躺在丈夫身边。没有你，其他都无所谓。她吞下了一剂苦毒，离开了这个世界，去找等待她的丈夫。

candidates.source: Okay, well, I was kinda out of it those first few days.  I knew there were storms, but I was having crazy fever dreams and stuff.  Honestly I probably should have gone to the hospital, except then I guess I'd be dead now.  I don't know what was a dream and what was the world ending.  I remember heading to the fridge for a drink and noticing the light was out and the water was warm, I think that was a bit before my fever broke.  I was still pretty groggy when I ran out of chicken soup, so it took me a while to really process how dark and dead my building was when I headed out.
candidates.target: 好吧，那前几天我有点神志不清。我知道有暴风雨，但我一直在做疯狂的发烧梦。老实说，我当时可能应该去医院的，不过如果那样的话，我现在可能就没命了。我分不清哪些是梦境，哪些是世界末日。我记得我去冰箱里拿饮料时，发现灯不亮了，水也变温了，我想那应该是我退烧之前的事情。当我用完鸡汤时，我还很迷糊，所以当我出门时，才发现整个大楼这么黑暗和死寂，我花了点时间才真正意识到。

candidates.source:
Understand that I'm not an expert about this."  The voice sighs.  You hear the person on the other side typing on a keyboard for several seconds.  "I will explain it as best I can, but again, I'm not a professional.  Whatever caused the apocalypse, it… broke something about the way our world works.  I'm sure you've noticed that 'normal' physics don't always apply anymore.  We are, as of right now, uncertain if our models were wrong, or if this is something fundamentally different to our reality."

"From what we've observed, these events are what happen at the peak of a cyclical effect.  This is gross oversimplification, and I don't know the science behind it, but… I guess the simplest way to think of it is that 'our' reality is moving closer and further from this other place, or model, or so on.  Like a yo-yo.  When these two things are closest together, we get portal storms.  Otherwise, things are… I wouldn't say normal, not anymore, but they are as close to normal as we get now."

"Reading a footnote here… we're looking to gather data about these storms using a device developed specifically for the purpose.  I'll add that to your contracts list, if you want to know more about it.
candidates.target:
“我明白我不是这个领域的专家。”声音里带着一丝叹息。你能听到对方敲击键盘的声音持续了几秒钟。“我会尽我所能解释，但再次强调，我不是专业人士。无论是什么原因导致了世界末日，它……改变了我们世界运作的方式。我确定你已经注意到，所谓的‘正常’物理定律不再总是适用。目前来说，我们不确定是我们的模型有误，还是这代表了我们现实中根本不同的事物。”

“根据我们的观察，这些事件发生在循环效应的高峰期。这是一个极其简化的说法，我也不了解背后的科学原理，但……我想最简单的说法就是，‘我们的’现实正在靠近或远离另一个地方、模型等等。就像玩耍悠悠球一样。当这两者最近时，我们就会遇到传送门风暴。其他时间，事情虽然不至于正常——现在已经不可能完全正常了——但它们尽可能地接近我们现在所能拥有的正常状态。”

“根据这里的脚注，我们正在使用专门开发的设备来收集这些风暴的数据。如果你想了解更多，我会把它添加到你的合同清单上。”

candidates.source: Not really.  The leadership fed us all kinds of conflicting stories, and there was some absolutely heinous stuff going on.  God, I still have nightmares.  I saw this one woman eat her own baby.  I don't know what it was about it, something about the look on her face.  Now we've both seen worse things with our own eyes, but that one still comes back to haunt me.  Anyway, they never could control the riots, and by the time the rioters started turning into undead it was way too late.  I don't know if morale just broke or what but I heard rumors it just became a free for all bloodletting.  What actually made the dead come back to life though?  I haven't got a clue.
candidates.target: 不，领导层给我们喂了各种互相矛盾的故事，当时有些极其可怕的事情正在发生。老天，我仍然会做噩梦。我看到一个女人吃自己的孩子。我不知道是什么让我如此难忘，也许是她脸上的表情。现在我们亲眼见过更糟糕的事情，但那一幕仍然让我挥之不去。反正他们永远无法控制骚乱，等到暴徒开始变成活死人时，已经太晚了。我不知道是士气崩溃还是其他原因，但我听说那时已经变成了一场全面的血腥屠杀。不过，到底是什么让死人复活的？我完全不知道。

candidates.source: You know, I'm kinda in the mood for some pub nachos right now.  The whole pub ambience would be good too, but I like how they'd put 'em on wax paper that'd be so soaked with cheese grease you could see right through it.  Those little black olive wheels that tasted like rubber, they were only ever good with pub nachos, you know?  Any other time, garbage.  I'd love to have a big tray of pub nachos, go to a karaoke night, and just sing fuckin' Abba songs until my throat hurt.  You in?
candidates.target: 你知道吗，我现在有点想吃酒吧纳乔。整个酒吧的氛围也很好，但我喜欢他们把纳乔放在蜡纸上，那种被奶酪油脂浸透到可以透过的蜡纸。那些像橡胶一样的小黑橄榄圈，除了和酒吧纳乔一起吃以外，其他时候都像垃圾一样难吃。我很想端着一大托盘酒吧纳乔，去参加卡拉OK之夜，然后一直唱阿巴乐队的歌，唱到喉咙痛。你一起去吗？

"We appreciate your thorough report," the voice finally responds.  "Your handling of the circumstances was commendable considering the anomalous and unpredictable nature of the facility.  If you seek further contract work, rest assured, we'll take into account the potential for anomalous circumstances in future assignments and relay them accordingly."

candidates.source: Died from sepsis a few weeks after you.  The cut on his leg that ultimately killed him would have been easily treatable in nearly any other situation.  His final wish was that he be allowed to drink himself into his grave.  Upon consideration, the party that he was with opted to shoot him in the head and divide his belongings rather than waste the alcohol.
candidates.target: 几周后，因败血症去世。最终导致他死亡的腿部伤口在几乎任何其他情况下都能轻易治疗。他的最后愿望是让自己喝到死。经过考虑，与他同在的聚会人员决定开枪打他的头，分他的财产，而不是浪费酒精。

candidates.source: Somehow, I don't know how, I managed to fall asleep in there.  I think it might have started with me hyperventilating and passing out.  When I woke up it was night, I was starving and parched, and… and the screaming had died down.  At first I tried to go out the way I came in, but I peaked out the window and saw one of the nurses stumbling around, spitting that black shit up.  Her name was Becky.  She wasn't Becky anymore.  So, I went back up and somehow made it into the storage area.  From there, the roof.  I drank water from some nasty old puddle and I camped out there for a while, watching the city around me burn.
candidates.target: 不知如何，我竟然在里面睡着了。我觉得可能是从我开始虚弱、晕倒开始的。当我醒来时，已经是夜晚，我又饿又渴，而且……尖叫声已经停了下来。起初我试图从我进来的地方出去，但我探出窗外，看到一个护士在四处晃悠，吐出黑色的东西。她叫贝基。她已经不是贝基了。于是，我回到楼上，不知如何竟然到了储藏室。从那里，我爬上了屋顶。我从一个脏旧的水洼里喝了点水，然后在那里扎营了一段时间，看着周围的城市燃烧。

candidates.source:
FROM: Bryan Rooters, Reception Manager
 TO: Receptionists
 RE: Housekeeping

 Hi team,
 Please be aware that the decision has been made to let go some of the housekeeping staff.
 This decision was made by management to ensure that our operation can run as smoothly and efficiently as possible by passing on these cost savings to the residents.
 To keep up with our high standards of elder care, I will be assigning some additional small tasks to you in the near future.
 As you know, here at Shady Hills we value each and every employee and see this as an excellent opportunity to grow, learn, and provide for the Shady Hills family.
 Please let me know if you have any questions.
 Thanks.
candidates.target:
来自：布莱恩·鲁特尔斯，前台经理
致：前台工作人员
主题：保洁

各位同事，

请注意，管理层已经决定裁掉部分保洁人员。

这个决定是为了确保我们的运营能够尽可能地顺利和高效，通过节省成本为居民提供更好的服务。

为了维持我们高标准的养老服务，我将在不久的将来为你们分配一些额外的轻微任务。

你们都知道，在Shady Hills，我们重视每一位员工，并认为这是一个成长、学习和为Shady Hills大家庭做出贡献的绝佳机会。

如有任何疑问，请随时告知我。

谢谢。

candidates.source: Well, I have this weird hope.  It's probably stupid, but I saw my fiancé peel out of there with his sister - my maid of honor - in her pickup truck as things went bad.  So, until I run into them again one way or another, I'm just gonna keep on believing they're out there, doing well.  That's more than most of us have.

candidates.source: There's the doc out front helping anyone that can pay… but for us up here, money mostly goes to food.  I could do a lot for basic cuts, bruises, and common stuff if I had some supplies to help out.  Could you bring me some antiseptic?  Six bottles would probably be enough to last us a while.

candidates.source: Okay, well, I was kinda out of it those first few days.  I knew there were storms, but I was having crazy fever dreams and stuff.  Honestly I probably should have gone to get help, except then I guess I'd be dead now.  I don't know what was a dream and what was the world ending.  I remember getting a drink and hearing some screaming far away, I think that was a bit before my fever broke.  I was still pretty groggy when I ran out of food, so it took me a while to really process how dead everything was when I headed out.
candidates.target: 好吧，那前几天我有点神志不清。我知道有暴风雨，但我一直在做疯狂的发烧梦之类的事。老实说，我可能应该去求助的，不过那样的话我现在可能就死了。我不知道哪些是梦，哪些是世界末日。我记得我去拿了点喝的，还听到了远处的尖叫声，我想那是发烧好转之前的事。当我跑完食物时我还很迷糊，所以我花了些时间才真正意识到一切都死了，当我出门时。

candidates.source: At first I wanted to help.  The riots, the fighting, it was too much for me to just sit back and listen to the chaos.  Then a buddy of mine visited me.  He'd been hurt and he wasn't making much sense, but what he told me… well, you can imagine the kind of stuff he told me.  Everything the worst of the story tellers was making up, and more.  Instead of packing up to try to fight, I took his advice and packed up to leave.  I was out at the edge and the riots hadn't reached me yet, but from what I'd heard it was smarter to get out than to hold tight.  I slipped out that night and camped a few days in the woods, waiting for it to blow over.  It never did.
candidates.target: 起初我想帮助。骚乱、战斗，我不能只是坐着听着混乱。然后一个朋友来看我。他受伤了，说的话也不太清楚，但他告诉我的……你可以想象他告诉我的那些事。故事里最糟糕的部分都是编造的，甚至更多。而不是收拾行李去战斗，我听从了他的建议，收拾行李离开了。我在边缘，骚乱还没到达我，但根据我听到的，离开比坚持更明智。我那晚偷偷溜走，在树林里露营了几天，等待它过去。它从来没有过去。

candidates.source: She was at home when the bombs started dropping and the world went to hell.  I was at work.  I tried to make it to our house, but the city was a war zone.  Things I can't describe lurching through the streets, crushing people and cars.  Soldiers trying to stop them, but hitting people in the crossfire as much as anything.  And then the collateral damage would get right back up and join the enemy.  If it hadn't been for my wife, I would have just left, but I did what I could and I slipped through.  I actually made it alive.
candidates.target: 当炸弹开始落下，世界陷入地狱时，她在家里。我在工作。我试图回到我们的房子，但城市已经变成了战场。我无法形容的东西在街上移动，压碎人们和汽车。士兵们试图阻止它们，但在交火中伤害了更多的人。然后，附带损害会重新站起来，加入敌人。如果不是因为我的妻子，我可能已经离开了，但我尽力而为，我设法穿过了。我实际上活了下来。

Things I can't describe lurching through the streets, crushing people and cars.  Soldiers trying to stop them, but hitting people in the crossfire as much as anything.  And then the collateral damage would get right back up and join the enemy.  If it hadn't been for my wife, I would have just left, but I did what I could and I slipped through.  I actually made it alive.

candidates.source: I lived alone, on the old family property way out in the middle of nowhere.  My husband passed away a bit over a month before this started… cancer.  If anything good has come out of all this, it's that I finally see a positive to losing him so young.  I'd been shut in for a while anyway.  When I heard about foreign weapons and sleeper agents, and rioting and such, I curled up with my woods soup and tried not to worry.
candidates.target: 我独自住在偏远的祖产上。我丈夫在这一切发生的前一个多月去世了……癌症。如果有什么好事发生，那就是我终于看到了他这么年轻就去世的积极一面。我反正已经关在家里一段时间了。当我听到关于外国武器、潜伏特工、骚乱等消息时，我蜷缩在我的森林汤里，尽量不去担心。

candidates.source: This is a deadland, you see.  Take a moment and look around, know what I mean?  What's left for you?  The dead will be in the fields, the forests, all over the world.  Anything that walks, they'll make it so it doesn't, and most will come back as undead.  Those that don't, the Enemy will change them as well.  Every deadland is the same.  You've years and more to go, but one way or another, this place is dead.  Though, as far as I can see, you've got quite a few years to go yet.
candidates.target: 这是一片死地，你看。花点时间环顾四周，你明白我的意思吗？还剩下什么给你？死者将在田野里，在森林里，遍布全球。任何活着的东西，他们都会让它不再活着，大多数还会变成活死人。那些没有变成活死人的，敌人也会改变他们。每一片死地都是一样的。你还有多年要走，但无论如何，这个地方已经死了。不过，从我看来，你还有很多年可以活。

candidates.source: That was when I had my old truck, the blue one.  We called 'er ol' yeller.  One time me an' Marty Gumps - or, as he were known to me, Rusty G - were drivin' ol' yeller up Mount Greenwood in the summertime, lookin' fer fireflies to catch.
candidates.target: 那是我有旧卡车的时候，那辆蓝色的。我们叫它“老黄”。有一次，我和马蒂·甘普——或者说，我叫他锈老G——在夏天开着老黄上格林伍德山，去抓萤火虫。

candidates.source:
OGRE INFESTATION!

Bridgewater officials have reported there are ogres nesting in the Hockomock Swamp area and local residents are urged to avoid the swamps until they can be dealt with.  "I know what people say on the internet, but they're wrong", said Bridgewater police spokesman Neal Riley.  "Ogres are not people like humans or dwarves are.  There are no baby ogres.  They don't grow up, they don't have families, they just show up out of nowhere and start eating people.  They're a menace."  Anyone with a verifiable ogre sighting is urged to call 508-555-9523 and report the information.

Somehow doesn't seem to be too contagious, I got tons of it on me… still not a zombie.  And then there are those goopy monsters around, whatever they are, I think they're connected.  Maybe they're behind it, or maybe they're something else caused by the same stuff.  Dunno, but mark my words: it's the goop.
candidates.target: 那些僵尸只是吐着它。眼、鼻、口里都吐出黑色的粘液。无论它是什么，都是让它们再次行走的东西。似乎并不太传染，我身上沾了很多...还是没变成僵尸。还有那些粘液怪物，无论它们是什么，我觉得它们有联系。也许它们是幕后黑手，或者它们是同一物质引起的另一种东西。不知道，但记住我的话：是粘液。

candidates.source: I thought I had those damned bugs figured out.  I got braver, started heading out by day more and more.  A bunch of deer and a bear had turned and chased me down.  It was brutal.  I got out of there, but I had to leave everything and start over.
candidates.target: 我以为我已经搞清楚了那些该死的虫子。我变得勇敢起来，白天出门的次数越来越多。一群鹿和一只熊突然转过身来追我。那真是太残酷了。我逃脱了，但我不得不放弃一切，重新开始。

candidates.source: So I get the boat and it moves smooth as silk across the lake, no sound or vibration but the waves against the hull.  I never see anyone or anything guiding the boat or making it move.  Anyway we arrived at an island in the lake and as we approached I can hear laughter and music.  Once we landed, they had me sign a contract which I'd figured would just be an NDA not to talk about the rich peoples party island.  Turns out I signed a contract to play music every night for three months for the price of room and board.
candidates.target: 于是我上了船，它像丝绸一样平滑地滑过湖面，除了船体与波浪的碰撞，没有声音或振动。我没有看到任何人或任何东西引导船只或让它移动。无论如何，我们到达了湖中的一个岛屿，当我们靠近时，我听到了笑声和音乐。我们登陆后，他们让我签署了一份合同，我原本以为只是一份关于不透露富人派对岛屿的保密协议。结果，我签署了一份合同，同意每个晚上演奏音乐三个月，以获得住宿和餐饮。

candidates.source: Ha, I don't fully understand it myself.  Those first few days were a tough time to be outside, that's for sure.  I got caught in one of those hellish rainstorms, it started to burn my skin right off and wrecked my tent.  I managed to take shelter under a tree, lying on top of my tent.  Wrecked the damn thing, but better it than me.  From what I hear, though, I got lucky.  That was pretty much the worst I saw.  I didn't run into any of those really big demon-monsters that I hear attacked, so I guess I got off lucky.
candidates.target: 哈，我自己也不完全明白。那些最初的几天，户外确实是个艰难的环境。我遇到了场地狱般的暴风雨，雨点像烧我的皮肤一样，还把我的帐篷毁了。我只能躲在树下，躺在帐篷上。虽然把帐篷毁了，但总比我自己好。据我所知，我算是运气好了。那算是我遇到的最糟糕的事情了。我没有遇到那些听说中会攻击人的巨大恶魔怪物，所以我算是幸运的。

candidates.source: Okay, well, I know this sounds like an Indiana Jones B-plot, but I think someone found Pandora's Box, the actual thing or close to it.  I think they tried to somehow harness it, to use the power in it for something.  Maybe even something good, who knows, the power of the gods seems like it would be a green energy source to me.  Whatever it was, they screwed it up, and released it for real.  Not just a metaphorical thing like in the stories, but actually set the forces of Hades loose on Earth.  Yeah, I know it's far-fetched, but like I said: I think I get a pass on that.

When I heard about foreign weapons and sleeper agents, and rioting and such, I curled up with my woods soup and tried not to worry.

candidates.source: She sure was, helped me through some very hard times in my life.  I used to be bullied in middle school, whenever I'd get beat up, she'd always help clean me up and tell me I'd be alright.  She had this recipe for peach casserole too, best one in the world.  It was hard for me when she passed, but I found some solace right here in this Church.  We'd always been religious, but this one just clicked for me, ya know?
candidates.target: 她确实是，在我人生最艰难的时刻帮助了我。我在中学时曾被欺负，每次被打后，她总是帮我清理伤口，告诉我一切都会好起来的。她还有一个桃子烩菜的食谱，是世界上最好的。当她去世时，我很难过，但我在这座教堂里找到了安慰。我们一直很虔诚，但这座教堂对我来说特别有意义，你知道的？

candidates.source: My chief responsibility is to monitor radio traffic and locate potential targets to secure or rescue.  The majority of radio repeaters are down and those that are working have only emergency power.  If you have a basic understanding of electronics you should be able to fabricate the 'radio repeater mod' found in these plans.  When this mod is attached to a radio station's main terminal, all short range radio traffic on emergency channels is boosted so we can pick it up at much longer ranges.  I really need you make me one.
candidates.target: 我的主要职责是监控无线电交通并定位潜在的目标以确保安全或救援。大多数无线电中继器已经失效，而仍在工作的则只有紧急电力。如果你对电子学有基本的了解，应该能够根据这些计划制作“无线电中继器修补件”。当这个修补件连接到无线电站的主终端时，所有在紧急频道上的短距离无线电交通都会被增强，这样我们就能接收到更远距离的信号。我真的需要你为我制作一个。

candidates.source: Okay, well, I know this sounds like an old children's story, but I think someone found Pandora's Box, the actual thing or close to it.  I think they tried to somehow harness it, to use the power in it for something.  Maybe even something good, who knows, the power of the gods seems like it would be handy to have around.  Whatever it was, they screwed it up, and released it for real.  Not just a metaphorical thing like in the stories, but actually set the forces of Hades loose on Earth.  Yeah, I know it's far-fetched, but like I said: I think I get a pass on that.
candidates.target: 好吧，我知道这听起来像是一个老掉牙的童话故事，但我认为有人找到了潘多拉的盒子，或者接近它真实存在的东西。我认为他们试图以某种方式驾驭它，利用里面力量去做某事。也许甚至是件好事，谁知道呢，拥有神的力量似乎会很有用。无论是什么，他们搞砸了，真的释放了它。不仅仅是像故事里那样比喻的东西，而是真正地将哈迪斯（冥王）的力量放到了地球上。是的，我知道这听起来很荒唐，但正如我所说：我认为我可以得到这样的豁免。

candidates.source: Depends on your definition.  I'm alive, aren't I?  When Hell itself came down from the skies and monsters started attacking the cities, I grabbed my stuff and got to my hideout.  But I still saw some stuff from where I was.  I watched those things stride past.  I still have nightmares about the way their bodies moved, like they broke the world just to be here.  I had nothing better to do.  I watched them rip up those goons with weapons, watched the dead rise back up and start fighting the living.  I watched a nice old lady rip the head off a dog.  I saw a body twitch and grow into some kind of electrified hulk beast.  I watched it all happen.
candidates.target: 取决于你的定义。我还活着，不是吗？当地狱从天而降，怪物开始攻击城市时，我抓起我的东西，躲进了我的藏身之处。但我还是从我所在的地方看到了些事情。我看着那些东西大步走过。我仍然会做噩梦，梦到它们移动的方式，仿佛它们只是为了存在而打破了世界。我没什么更好的事可做。我看着它们用武器撕裂那些恶棍，看着死者复活并开始攻击活着的人。我看着一位和蔼的老太太撕下一条狗的头。我看到一具尸体抽搐着，长成一种电击的怪物野兽。我看着这一切都发生。

candidates.source: “Plato had defined man as an animal, biped and featherless, and was applauded. Diogenes \[of Sinope] plucked a fowl and brought it into the lecture-room with the words: Here is Plato's man. In consequence of which there was added to the definition: having broad nails.” \n— Diogenes Laertius (“The Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers”, “Diogenes”, sec. 40)
candidates.target:
柏拉图将人定义为没有羽毛的两足动物，并得到了赞誉。但狄奥根尼（西诺普的）将一只鸡的羽毛拔掉，带进了讲座室，说：“这是柏拉图的人。” 因此，定义中又增加了“指甲宽”这一条。
— 狄奥根尼·拉埃尔提乌斯（《著名哲学家生平、观点与语录》，《狄奥根尼》，第40节）

candidates.source: “Plato had defined man as an animal, biped and featherless, and was applauded. Diogenes \[of Sinope] plucked a fowl and brought it into the lecture-room with the words: Here is Plato's man. In consequence of which there was added to the definition: having broad nails.” \n— Diogenes Laertius (“The Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers”, “Diogenes”, sec. 40)
candidates.target:
柏拉图将人定义为一种两足、没有羽毛的动物，并因此受到赞扬。底格里斯（辛诺珀人）拔了一只鸟的羽毛，带着它走进讲堂，说：“这就是柏拉图定义的人。” 因此，在定义中又加上了“有宽大的指甲”这一条。
—— 狄奥金尼·拉耳提乌斯，《著名哲学家列传》，“底格里斯”，第40段

candidates.source: “Plato had defined man as an animal, biped and featherless, and was applauded. Diogenes \[of Sinope] plucked a fowl and brought it into the lecture-room with the words: Here is Plato's man. In consequence of which there was added to the definition: having broad nails.” \n— Diogenes Laertius (“The Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers”, “Diogenes”, sec. 40)
candidates.target:
柏拉图曾将人定义为一种两足无羽的动物，并因此受到赞扬。狄俄根尼[西诺普的]拔下一只禽类的羽毛，把它带到讲堂上，说道：“这就是柏拉图的人。” 结果，人们在定义中增加了“有宽大的指甲”这一条。

— 狄俄根尼·拉尔修（《名哲传》，“狄俄根尼”，第40节）

candidates.source: “Plato had defined man as an animal, biped and featherless, and was applauded. In consequence of which there was added to the definition: having broad nails.” \n— Diogenes Laertius (“The Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers”, “Diogenes”, sec. 40)
candidates.target:
柏拉图将人定义为一种动物，双足且没有羽毛，并得到了赞扬。狄奥格尼修（狄奥格尼修）从一个鸟类中取出一只，并将其带入讲堂，他说：“这就是柏拉图所说的‘人’。”因此，定义中又增加了“指甲宽大”的描述。

— 狄奥格尼修《贤哲传记》（“狄奥格尼修”卷，第40节）

candidates.source: “Plato had defined man as an animal, biped and featherless, and was applauded. Diogenes \[of Sinope] plucked a fowl and brought it into the lecture-room with the words: Here is Plato's man. In consequence of which there was added to the definition: having broad nails.” \n— Diogenes Laertius (“The Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers”, “Diogenes”, sec. 40)

candidates.source: You deposit the sheet in the tray.  After a long silence, the tray opens again, this time with a pile of coins.  "Astounding!  These conditions are clearly Earth-like, but the recordings performed unexpected loops in its subroutines.  The topographical scan shows what appear to be deliberate patterns in the placement of whatever structures you may have encountered.  We suspect that this may be a location where spacetime is slipping in various directions.  We will forward this to Research and alert you if we need more scans."
candidates.target: 你将纸张放入托盘。经过一段长时间的沉默，托盘再次打开，这次托盘里多了一堆硬币。“令人惊叹！这些条件明显是地球般的，但是记录显示在子程序中执行了意外的循环。地形扫描显示，你可能遇到的结构的布局似乎是有意形成的图案。我们怀疑这里可能是时空在不同方向上扭曲的地点。我们会将此信息转发给研究部门，如果需要更多扫描，我们会通知你。”

candidates.source: &Before you stands a towering mass of metal, at least seven feet high, with a large reflective glass plate in the center of its torso.  It turns as you enter the room, and raises its hand in a surprisingly natural motion of greeting.  A gravelly voice resonates from unseen speakers in the steel frame.  Its tone is bizarrely normal, in complete contrast with everything else around you.  "Oy, you ain't dead.  Lookin' t'trade?"  The accent sounds vaguely British, but not familiar; like a terrible imitation of Cockney.
candidates.target: 在你面前矗立着一座至少有七英尺高的金属巨塔，它的胸口中央有一块大大的反光玻璃板。它转过身来，当你进入房间时，它以出乎意料自然的问候动作举起手。从钢制框架中隐形的扬声器传出沙哑的声音。它的语调奇异地正常，与你周围的一切形成鲜明对比。“喂，你没死。想交易吗？”口音听起来有点像英国口音，但又不熟悉；像是一个糟糕的伦敦东区口音模仿。

candidates.source: Besides the acid rain, I mostly saw people fleeing the cities.  I tried to stay away from the roads, but I didn't want to get lost in the woods either, so I stuck to the deep margins.  I saw cars, buses, trucks loaded down with evacuees.  Plenty went right on, but a lot stalled out of gas and other stuff.  Some were so full of gear and people there were folks hanging off them.  Stalling out was a death sentence, because the dead were coming along the roads picking off the survivors.
candidates.target: 除了酸雨之外，我看到大部分人都在逃离城市。我尽量避开道路，但也不想在森林里迷路，所以我走在路边深处。我看到汽车、公交车、卡车装满了撤离的人。很多车继续前行，但也有很多因为没油和其他原因而抛锚。有些车上装满了物品和人，甚至有人在车外挂着。抛锚就意味着死刑，因为死者沿着道路寻找幸存者。

candidates.source:
After so long spent experimenting on vampire blood, I found a way to push vampirism beyond its absolute limits.
By taking vampire blood, a drop of my own blood, some blood no human nor vampire could ever want to drink and an assortment of poisons and toxins, it is possible to apply the process of an ancient poison-making method to vampire blood, forcing it to devour itself to become stronger.
When the process was over and I drank the remaining blood, I could now drink vampire blood to become more of a vampire than they are, with all the power this brings.
candidates.target: 经过长时间的吸血鬼血液实验，我找到了一种将吸血鬼能力推向极限的方法。通过混合吸血鬼血液、我自己的血液、没有任何人类或吸血鬼愿意饮用的血液以及各种毒素和有毒物质，我可以应用一种古老的制毒方法来处理吸血鬼血液，迫使它自我消耗以变得更强。当过程完成后，我喝下了剩余的血液，现在我可以喝吸血鬼血液，成为比他们更强大的“吸血鬼”，并拥有随之而来的所有力量。

candidates.source: I kind of lost track of the days.  Every day was the same; eat, check the barricades, look on the Internet, play some games with the sound off to try and distract myself.  I filled up my bathtub, and once the water went out, I'd drink from there with a lifestraw when I needed to hydrate.  Meal planning got easier after I was down to just my canned stuff.  The Internet didn't stay on for long, though, which I guess was a blessing because of how many people were sharing their fear and awful experiences in real time.  I did that routine every day until that emergency broadcast came through that no help was coming, and then I knew it was over.
candidates.target: 我有点失去了对日期的感知。每一天都一样；吃饭、检查路障、上网、玩一些静音游戏来分散注意力。我把浴缸装满水，水用完了，我就用吸管从那里喝水来补充水分。当我只剩下罐头食物时，制定餐食计划变得更容易了。然而，互联网并没有持续很久，这可能是一个祝福，因为有很多人在实时分享他们的恐惧和可怕的经历。我每天都重复这个例行公事，直到紧急广播说没有援助了，然后我知道一切都结束了。

candidates.source:
&The Doc lays you down on the bed and tells you not to move.  The last thing you see is the robotic arm of the device slowly descend toward your neck.  A syringe full of some liquid is then plunged into your skin, and you wake up, resting in a silent room.

You reach behind your ear and feel a bandage - underneath is a small metal port, and your fingers can make out several bumps that feel like USB connections.  The doctor sees you and grins.

"Ah, great, you're up.  All done.  If we get any new implants from the Hub, you'll be free to come by and buy them.  Otherwise, happy to install any you can scavenge from those killer robots.  Just make sure they're packaged and sterile."
candidates.target:
医生把你放到床上，告诉你不要动。你看到的最后一件事是设备的机械手臂缓缓降到你的脖子上。然后，一根装满某种液体的注射器刺入你的皮肤，你醒来时，躺在一个安静的房间里。

你伸手摸到耳朵后边，感觉到一个绷带——下面是一个小金属端口，你的手指能摸到几个像USB连接的突起。医生看到你，咧嘴一笑。

“啊，好，你醒了。都完成了。如果我们从中心得到新的植入物，你可以随时来买。否则，很高兴为你安装你从那些杀手机器人那里抢到的任何植入物。只是确保它们是包装好的，无菌的。”

candidates.source:
In addition to manifesting more of the vampires' classical weaknesses, some time after beginning to consume vampires for power the sun's rays started to ignite me, as I found the hard way when a fight lasted longer than planned.
My powers barely did anything to block them and I had to sink below the earth to survive that day.
I did felt a passing impulse to drink more vampire blood and the first few doses made me think my mind would unravel, but that passed.  It might be that this path gives a single weakness not seen in other vampires to those far enough on it, but testing this would require creating vampires and I won't ever tolerate this.
candidates.target: 除了展现出对吸血鬼的经典弱点外，在开始以吸血鬼为食物来增强力量的一段时间后，太阳的光线开始燃烧我，这是在一场战斗持续时间比预期长时我以硬方式发现的。我的力量几乎无法阻挡它们，我只能潜入地下才能活过那一天。我确实有过一个短暂的冲动想要喝更多的吸血鬼血，前几次让我觉得我的思维会崩溃，但这很快就过去了。也许这条道路会给那些走得足够远的人带来其他吸血鬼没有的单一弱点，但测试这一点需要创造出吸血鬼，而我永远不会容忍这样做。
